name: Cyclamen
grown_as: The hardy autumn-flowering cyclamen, ivy-leaved sowbread. William has a pink one and a white one in the rockery; drawn pink.
habit: A low mound 10 to 15 cm high. In late summer the flowers come up on their own from a bare tuber at the soil surface; the marbled leaves follow and stay all winter, dying away in early summer.

leaf.arrangement: Many leaves, each on its own long stalk from the top of the tuber, forming a low mound
leaf.outline: Heart-shaped to triangular, often with a few shallow angular lobes like an ivy leaf, 4 to 12 cm long; very variable
leaf.base: Heart-shaped (cordate), deeply notched where the stalk joins
leaf.margin: Smooth or with small, shallow, widely spaced teeth
leaf.veins: Palmate from the stalk; not prominent
leaf.surface: Dark green above, marbled with a silver-grey pattern (often a band shaped like an arrowhead or a ring); underside often reddish-purple
leaf.stalk: Long, thin, reddish, curving up from the tuber

flower.form: A nodding flower with its petals swept straight back upwards, like a shuttlecock
flower.petals: Five petals, joined at the base into a short tube, the lobes long and narrow, bent sharply back up and slightly twisted
flower.centre: At the mouth a deeper magenta V-shaped mark on each petal, and small ear-like flaps (auricles) at each petal base; the mouth points down
flower.carried: Alone on a thin stalk 10 to 15 cm from the tuber, the stalk curving over at the top so the flower hangs, its petals pointing up
flower.season: August to October, before or with the first leaves

fruit: After flowering the stalk coils like a spring from the top down, pulling the round capsule (about 1 cm) to the soil under the leaves. It opens the next summer to show sticky seeds that ants carry away.
seedling: Not drawn. One small round seed leaf above a tiny tuber.
winter: At its best: a mound of marbled leaves all winter.

leaf: heart-shaped to ivy-shaped, with a deep notch at the base
dark green with a silver-grey marbled pattern
bloom: five petals swept straight back upwards from a hanging flower
a deep magenta V at the mouth of each petal
small ear-like flaps at the base of the petals
bulb: a tuber, not a bulb: a flattened, corky brown disc, often large
roots from the top and sides as well as below
shoots from the middle of the top
shoots: flower stalks coming up from the bare tuber before the leaves
young leaves unrolling from the top of the tuber
flower: pink shuttlecock flowers on thin stalks over a low mound
marbled heart-shaped leaves round them, or not yet up
seedhead: round seed pods pulled down to the soil under the leaves
dormant: the top of the bare tuber showing at the soil surface

look_alikes: Cyclamen coum flowers in winter, with short rounded petals, no ear-like flaps at the base and round, unlobed leaves. Florists' cyclamen (C. persicum) is much bigger and not hardy. The leaves can be taken for ivy, but ivy climbs and has woody stems.
